mechanism_narrative: Persistent decline in WORKPLACES mobility (from -24.0% to -29.4% over four weeks) signals sustained remote work adoption and reduced commuting. This suppresses incidental retail visits during commute windows, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined 5.4 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points in the next four weeks despite WORKPLACES remaining below -25%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL mobility (9.7% to 14.3% over four weeks) indicates households consolidating at home. This behavioral shift reduces discretionary retail trips as consumers substitute home-based activities for out-of-home recreation, causing RETAIL_REC to decline further.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL increased 4.6 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -40% in the next four weeks while RESIDENTIAL remains above 13%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility collapse (from -40.6% to -50.0%) signals public transport restrictions or reduced service. When TRANSIT falls below -48%, retail accessibility via mass transit becomes severely constrained, triggering a threshold effect that suppresses RETAIL_REC recovery over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -48% in current week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -50.0% in t-0w, lowest in series
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 8 percentage points in the two weeks following TRANSIT reaching -50%.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between declining TRANSIT (-50.0%) and declining WORKPLACES (-29.4%) creates a dual-constraint regime: reduced commuting combined with transport unavailability eliminates the primary driver of retail foot traffic. This interaction effect suppresses RETAIL_REC recovery more strongly than either factor alone.
evidence_refs: fact:both series at multi-week lows simultaneously
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 10 percentage points over the next four weeks when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain in the specified constraint regime.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility volatility (4.4% to -2.6% over four weeks) reflects weather-dependent outdoor activity patterns in Melbourne autumn. When PARKS mobility turns negative, consumers redirect discretionary time indoors to retail venues, producing a compensatory increase in RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines below 0% in current week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 29.7% at t-2w to -2.6% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below -45% in the week following PARKS turning negative.

mechanism_narrative: Stable GROCERY_PHARM mobility (around -7% to -8%) indicates maintained essential shopping discipline. When essential shopping remains suppressed despite overall mobility decline, it signals strong behavioral compliance with restrictions, which extends to retail-recreation suppression, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains between -6% and -9% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stable at -8.7%, -6.1%, -7.0%, -7.9% across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above -35% in the next four weeks while GROCERY_PHARM remains in the -6% to -9% band.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between RESIDENTIAL elevation (14.3%) and PARKS suppression (-2.6%) indicates households are staying home rather than visiting outdoor recreation. This substitution of home for out-of-home activity reduces retail incidence, as consumers consolidate shopping trips and minimize discretionary visits.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 14.3% and PARKS at -2.6% in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 6 percentage points in the next two weeks when RESIDENTIAL exceeds 13% and PARKS is negative.

mechanism_narrative: Cumulative four-week deterioration across TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and RETAIL_REC (all at multi-week lows) indicates escalating mobility restrictions. If this restriction regime persists unchanged, RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed at current levels; recovery requires observable reversal in TRANSIT or WORKPLACES within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both decline week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:all three series at or near four-week lows in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 12 percentage points in the next week when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both decline week-on-week.
